faq.q: Is it okay to feel upset after a setback?
faq.a: Yes. Feeling sad, cross or disappointed is normal. Resilience is not about hiding feelings; it is about feeling them and then finding a way forward.
asks: Should I hide that I am upset?

faq.a: Caring people to talk to, a plan with small steps, kind self-talk, and looking after your body with sleep, food and exercise all help people bounce back.
asks: How do I bounce back after failing?

faq.a: Resilience is the ability to cope when things go wrong and to bounce back, often stronger and wiser than before.
Resilience is more like a muscle than a gift. Anyone can grow it through practice and support, especially from caring adults and friends.
asks: Can I learn to be resilient?

faq.q: What if I cannot bounce back on my own?
faq.a: You do not have to. Bouncing back is easier with help, so talk to a trusted grown-up, a teacher, a school counsellor or a doctor if things feel too heavy.
asks: I keep failing and feel stuck

facts: Psychologist Emmy Werner followed nearly 700 children on the Hawaiian island of Kauai for decades and found that a caring adult helped many bounce back from hard starts.
Basketball star Michael Jordan was not picked for his high school's top team in his second year, and later became one of the greatest players ever.
